questions.text: Have you ever been formally diagnosed with eczema (atopic dermatitis), hay fever (allergic rhinitis), or allergic asthma?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; Atopic March literature (Spergel 2010)

questions.text: Do any of your biological parents or siblings have eczema, hay fever, or asthma?

responses.label: Yes, two or more first-degree relatives

questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; Lubs 1971 (atopy heritability ~50–75%)

questions.text: How would you rate your eczema (skin dryness, itching, rash) over the past 4 weeks?

responses.label: Severe (constant itch, significant sleep loss, skin cracking)

questions.source: OMICS Eczema Report; POEM score (Charman 2004)

questions.text: Do you experience dry, itchy, or red eyes without infection (not attributable to screen fatigue)?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Eczema Assessment; Dry-eye as atopic/autoimmune marker

questions.text: How severely does hay fever (sneezing, runny/blocked nose, itchy eyes) affect you during peak season?

responses.label: Severely affected (prescription or daily meds, limits activity)

triggers.if_response: Severely affected (prescription or daily meds, limits activity)

questions.source: OMICS Hay Fever Assessment; TNSS (Total Nasal Symptom Score)

questions.text: How well-controlled is your asthma? (If not diagnosed with asthma, skip)

responses.label: Well controlled (symptoms ≤2 days/week, no night waking)
Partially controlled (symptoms >2 days/week or any night waking)

questions.source: OMICS Asthma Report; ACQ (Asthma Control Questionnaire, Juniper 1999)

questions.text: Do you have a confirmed food allergy or severe food intolerance (not a preference)?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; WAO Food Allergy Guidelines 2023

questions.text: Do you have diagnosed psoriasis or recurring scaly, silvery skin plaques?
questions.source: OMICS Inflammation Report; Neimann 2006 (psoriasis–CVD link)

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with lupus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), or another systemic autoimmune condition?

responses.label: Other systemic autoimmune (ankylosing spondylitis, vasculitis, etc.)

questions.source: OMICS Inflammation Report; ACR Lupus/RA criteria

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with Hashimoto's thyroiditis or Graves' disease (autoimmune thyroid)?
questions.source: OMICS Thyroid Report; Thyroid peroxidase antibody prevalence data

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis (inflammatory bowel disease)?
questions.source: OMICS GI Report; ECCO IBD Guidelines 2023

questions.text: Do you experience persistent shortness of breath, morning cough, or wheeze unrelated to asthma?

responses.label: Mild — slight breathlessness on significant exertion
Moderate — breathless on hills/stairs, some daily limitation
Severe — breathless on minimal exertion, daily cough/sputum

questions.source: OMICS Respiratory Report; MRC Dyspnoea Scale; GOLD COPD Guidelines 2023

questions.text: Do you have persistent nasal congestion, facial pressure, or post-nasal drip lasting more than 12 weeks?
questions.source: EPOS 2020 Sinusitis Guidelines; OMICS Allergy Assessment

questions.text: How many colds or flu-like illnesses have you had in the past 12 months?
questions.source: OMICS Immunity Assessment; Hemila 2013 (vitamin C/zinc immune function)

questions.text: Have any recent blood tests shown elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR, white cell count)?
questions.source: OMICS Inflammation Report; Ridker 2003 (hsCRP cardiovascular risk)

questions.text: Are you regularly exposed to pets (fur/dander) or a dusty, mould-prone home environment?

responses.label: Cat or dog in the home
Mould / damp in home or workplace

questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; Custovic 2000 (allergen exposure dose–response)

questions.text: Are you regularly exposed to second-hand smoke at home or work?

responses.label: Regularly (weekly, e.g. smoky workplace or partner smokes)

questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; US Surgeon General SHS Report 2006

questions.text: How many courses of antibiotics have you taken in the past 2 years?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Eczema Assessment; Blaser 2011 (antibiotics and atopy); Arrieta 2015

questions.text: Do you experience gut symptoms such as bloating, loose stools, urgency, or abdominal cramping most weeks?

responses.label: Mild — occasional, not impacting daily life
Moderate — most weeks, some impact on daily life
Severe — most days, significant impact (e.g. rushing to toilet)

questions.source: OMICS GI Report; Rome IV IBS/IBD criteria

questions.text: How many portions of vegetables, legumes, or whole grains do you eat per day?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Eczema Assessment; Trompette 2014 (dietary fibre–immune axis)

questions.text: How often do you eat processed red meat, fried foods, or butter-heavy meals?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; Calder 2017 (dietary fat and inflammation)

questions.text: How often do you eat oily fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel, herring)?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Eczema/Hay Fever Assessment; Calder 2013 (omega-3 and allergy)

questions.text: Do you currently avoid dairy products? (allergy, intolerance, or dietary choice)

responses.label: Yes — due to diagnosed dairy allergy or intolerance

questions.source: OMICS Allergy Assessment; Kiefte-de Jong 2012 (dairy and allergy outcomes)

questions.text: How much direct sunlight does your skin receive on most days?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Eczema Assessment; Baeke 2010 (vitamin D and immune regulation)

questions.text: Do psychological stress or poor sleep noticeably worsen your skin, allergies, or gut symptoms?

responses.label: Almost always — stress is a major trigger

questions.source: OMICS Eczema/IBD Reports; Dhabhar 2014 (stress and immune dysregulation)

questions.text: Do you have persistent joint pain, morning stiffness, or swelling in multiple joints (not from injury)?

responses.label: Moderate — daily stiffness >1 hour, activity affected
Severe — constant pain, swollen joints, prescribed biologic/DMARD

triggers.if_response: Moderate — daily stiffness >1 hour, activity affected
Severe — constant pain, swollen joints, prescribed biologic/DMARD

questions.source: OMICS Inflammation Report; ACR RA Classification Criteria 2010

questions.text: Are you currently taking any medications for immune or inflammatory conditions?
questions.source: OMICS Medication Review; NHS BNF steroid side-effect profile

questions.text: How would you describe your skin between eczema flares (or in general if no eczema)?

responses.label: Generally normal — not particularly dry or sensitive
Mildly dry or sensitive — prone to redness
Persistently dry, flaky, or reactive (to soaps/detergents)

triggers.if_response: Persistently dry, flaky, or reactive (to soaps/detergents)

questions.source: OMICS Eczema Assessment; Elias 2008 (skin barrier and atopic march)

questions.text: Are you immune-suppressed due to a medical condition or treatment (chemotherapy, organ transplant, HIV, long-term corticosteroids)?

responses.label: Mild / secondary (long-term low-dose corticosteroids, mild CVID)

questions.source: OMICS Immunity Report; WHO immunodeficiency classification

questions.text: Are you regularly exposed at work to dust, fumes, chemicals, latex, or animal allergens?

responses.label: Low — occasional mild exposure (office, light dust)
High — regular exposure (construction, chemical, lab, farming, bakery)

questions.source: OMICS Respiratory Report; Tarlo 2008 (occupational asthma review)

questions.text: Do you take a vitamin D supplement?
questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Immunity Assessment; Martineau 2017 (vitamin D RCT meta-analysis)

questions.text: Do you take an omega-3 (fish oil / algae oil) supplement?

responses.label: No, and eat little oily fish
No, but eat oily fish regularly
Yes, regular omega-3 supplement (≥1 g EPA+DHA/day)

questions.source: OMICS Allergy/Eczema/Psoriasis Reports; Calder 2013 (omega-3 anti-inflammatory effects)

questions.text: At what age did your first allergic/atopic condition appear, and did others follow?

responses.label: Eczema in childhood progressing to hay fever
Full march: eczema → food allergy → hay fever → asthma

triggers.if_response: Full march: eczema → food allergy → hay fever → asthma

questions.source: Spergel 2010 (atopic march natural history); OMICS Allergy Assessment
